headline: Paraguay Country Risk Spikes Following President Peña's Resignation
summary: Paraguay's country risk premium rose 6.6% to 146 basis points following the resignation of President Santiago Peña amid a banking crisis at Ueno Bank. Sovereign bonds have fallen to their lowest levels since June 2025.
why: Sovereign risk premiums are critical for emerging market investors as they reflect the cost of government borrowing and overall political stability.

impacts.name: Paraguay
impacts.why: Political instability and bank failures increase default risk for sovereign debt.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The sudden resignation of the head of state combined with a domestic banking collapse creates significant uncertainty, triggering a sell-off in sovereign debt.
